newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Newcrest sees 96/97 gold output up.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Newcrest sees 96/97 gold output up.

text.p: Australian gold miner Newcrest Mining Ltd said on Wednesday it expected gold production to rise to between 586,000 to 590,000 ounces in the year to June 30, 1997, from 581,913 ounce in 1995/96.

"The difference this year is that we will not have the 66,000 ounces that we got out of Ora Banda so we are expecting a distinct improvement from (Newcrest's main mine) Telfer to compensate for that," managing director John Quinn said in a conference call.
The Ora Banda gold mine was sold for A$17 million in August.
Production from Telfer, located in Western Australia, slipped during fiscal 1995/96 due to lower head grades and commissioning problems with a leach pad.
But Quinn said the leach pad woes were expected to be mostly overcome this year.
Ore grades from Telfer were seen improving only slightly with some change in ore mixes expected to lead to a higher throughput rate for the higher grade underground material.
Costs per ounce of gold produced were seen falling, Quinn said.
"We would expect our costs in 1996/97 to come down off the overall average for the preceding year probably by (around) A$20 an ounce at current estimates," he said.
Price per ounce realised for fiscal 1996/97 gold sales was seen little changed from last year's level of A$631.
Newcrest's net profit after tax for the year to June 30, 1996 was A$20.8 million, about half that of a year earlier.
The company was hit by lower production and higher costs during the year.
Newcrest shares finished Wednesday down seven cents at A$4.93.
